title: Board of Supervisors Member (Information Technology Expert)
description:
Role Summary
The Board of Supervisors Member having Information Technology expertise shall provide strategic oversight, independent supervision, and expert guidance on the Bank's information technology infrastructure, digital transformation, cybersecurity, IT governance, technology risk management, and information systems.
The position requires an internationally experienced IT professional with substantial operational and strategic leadership experience in banking or regulated financial services. The member shall provide independent, evidence-based assurance to the Board of Supervisors (BoS) on whether technology services are reliable, secure, efficient, adequately resourced and aligned with business objectives, applicable regulations and operational resilience principles. Particular emphasis shall be placed on the stability and responsiveness of the core banking system and other critical services, recurring incidents, customer and staff experience, timely resolution of deficiencies and sustainable improvement in IT performance.
The member shall act in a non-executive capacity and exercise oversight through the BoS and its authorized committees. The Board of Management and Chief of IT retain responsibility for IT operations, staffing, incident resolution, implementation and service delivery. The member shall not issue routine operational instructions to staff, assume management functions or approve transactions outside delegated Board authority.

Duties and Responsibilities
A. IT Governance and Strategic Oversight
1. Provide strategic oversight of the Bank’s Oracle FLEXCUBE Core Banking System, ensuring its security, performance, reliability, integration, upgrades, and operational resilience.
2. Provide independent oversight of the Bank’s IT governance framework, policies, strategies, and technology investments.
3. Review the Bank’s IT strategy to ensure alignment with corporate objectives and business priorities.
4. Monitor the implementation of IT strategic initiatives, major technology projects, and digital transformation programmes.
5. Ensure accountability, transparency, and effective governance in the utilization of IT resources and investments.
6. Review significant IT proposals, expenditures, technology procurement, and vendor arrangements to ensure appropriate oversight and value for money.
7. Review IT organizational structure, staffing, technical competency, succession planning and dependency on key individuals or external vendors. Challenge whether resources and the Chief of IT's performance objectives are adequate for reliable service delivery, and recommend corrective measures to the BoS.
8. Review material IT investments against documented business cases, total cost of ownership, implementation milestones, service benefits and post-implementation results. Monitor vendor service commitments and escalation of persistent underperformance.
B. Cybersecurity and Information Security
Oversee the effectiveness of the Bank's cybersecurity governance and information security management framework.
Assess the adequacy of controls designed to protect the Bank against cyberattacks, data breaches, malware, ransomware, and other emerging threats.
Review cybersecurity risk assessments, vulnerability assessments, penetration testing results, and remediation plans.
Monitor the implementation of internationally recognized information security standards, particularly ISO/IEC 27001 and NIST Cybersecurity Framework.
Ensure appropriate oversight of information security incidents, response mechanisms, and recovery arrangements.
Seek independent assurance on the effectiveness of cybersecurity controls, including security monitoring, identity and privileged access management, patch management, vulnerability remediation, data protection and incident preparedness. Review the frequency, scope and results of independent security assessments and require management to present risk-prioritized remediation and evidence of closure.
C. IT Risk Management and Regulatory Compliance
Evaluate the Bank's IT risk management framework and ensure that technology-related risks are appropriately identified, assessed, monitored, and mitigated.
Oversee IT-related internal controls, access management, data protection, and information security arrangements.
Monitor compliance with applicable Da Afghanistan Bank regulations, directives, and other relevant regulatory requirements.
Review IT audit findings and ensure timely implementation of corrective actions.
Assess technology-related third-party, outsourcing, cloud computing, and vendor management risks.
Review material technology risk exceptions, overdue regulatory and audit findings, management's risk acceptance proposals and remediation evidence. Coordinate oversight with Risk Management, Compliance and Internal Audit without compromising their independence or duplicating their mandates.
D. Digital Banking and Technology Innovation
Provide strategic guidance on digital banking, mobile banking, internet banking, electronic payment systems, and financial technology solutions.
Assess emerging technologies, including Artificial Intelligence, cloud computing, automation, and data analytics, for their potential contribution to the Bank.
Support the development and implementation of secure, scalable, and customer-oriented digital banking solutions.
Provide oversight of technology initiatives supporting the Bank's Islamic banking operations and digital financial services.
Review the governance of new technology products, major releases and integrations, including documented risk and security assessments, business/user acceptance testing, readiness criteria, contingency arrangements and post-implementation reviews. Obtain assurance that material deficiencies are addressed before launch, subject to applicable approval authorities.
E. IT Infrastructure and Operational Resilience
Oversee the adequacy, reliability, scalability, and security of the Bank's IT infrastructure, networks, databases, servers, and core banking systems.
Review business continuity and disaster recovery arrangements, including critical-service recovery time and recovery point objectives (RTO/RPO), backup restoration tests, disaster recovery exercises, actual recovery results, dependencies and remediation of test failures.
Monitor the actual availability, responsiveness, capacity and reliability of critical services, including Oracle FLEXCUBE, databases, servers, network connectivity, branch systems, digital banking, ATMs, payment systems and interfaces. Review performance during peak business periods and compare actual results with approved service levels.
Ensure that appropriate technology resilience measures are in place to minimize operational disruptions.
Review the incident and problem management framework. For major or recurring incidents, scrutinize root-cause analyses, business and customer impact, duration, recovery actions, accountable owners, permanent corrective measures and evidence that recurrence risk has been reduced.
Review IT service desk and departmental feedback trends, including unresolved complaints, ticket aging, recurring issues, response and resolution times, service-level breaches and user satisfaction. Challenge persistent service quality problems and require time-bound management improvement plans through the BoS.
Assess the adequacy of capacity planning, infrastructure lifecycle management, preventive maintenance, system monitoring, change and release governance, and contingency arrangements. Review repeated or failed changes and the management response to obsolete or unsupported technology.
F. Board-Level Reporting and Oversight
Review a standardized monthly IT performance and risk dashboard submitted by management, with trends, approved targets, actual results, exceptions, business impact, action owners and deadlines. Present a consolidated assessment and recommendations to the BoS at least quarterly, or more frequently where material issues warrant.
Challenge management decisions where necessary to ensure appropriate technology governance and risk management.
Monitor the implementation of Board-approved IT strategies, recommendations, and corrective action plans.
Advise the Board on material technology risks, emerging cyber threats, and significant technological developments affecting the banking industry.
The dashboard shall, at a minimum, cover critical-service uptime and unplanned downtime; core banking response times and transaction failure rates; incident volume, severity, recurrence and mean time to restore service; service desk backlog and SLA compliance; cybersecurity risk indicators; backup and disaster recovery test results; overdue audit and regulatory actions; and material project, vendor and budget exceptions. Targets and escalation thresholds shall be proposed by management and approved through the applicable governance process.
Review significant incident notifications promptly and escalate material service disruptions, unresolved critical risks, repeated SLA breaches or overdue high-risk actions to the BoS Chairperson, in accordance with the Bank's escalation framework. Seek documented management responses, agreed corrective actions and evidence-based closure.
Obtain relevant performance reports and supporting information through authorized channels, and meet with the Chief of IT, relevant business functions and independent control functions as necessary. Where appropriate, recommend an independent technical assessment or external specialist review for BoS approval.
Maintain a record of IT oversight recommendations, BoS decisions, assigned management owners, deadlines, progress and independently validated closure where appropriate. Review unresolved high-priority matters at each relevant BoS or committee meeting.
Within the first 90 days of appointment, present an initial assessment of the Bank's IT service performance, infrastructure resilience, cybersecurity governance, IT organizational capability and material open issues, together with a prioritized improvement roadmap and proposed oversight calendar. Thereafter, review progress against the roadmap and provide an annual assessment of IT oversight effectiveness.

Job Requirements
Educational Qualifications
The candidate must meet the following educational requirements, subject to applicable regulatory eligibility criteria:
A Bachelor's Degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Software Engineering or a closely related discipline from a recognized and accredited university is required. A relevant Master's Degree is strongly preferred. A candidate without a Master's Degree may be considered where substantial relevant senior banking IT experience and recognized professional credentials demonstrate equivalent capability, subject to applicable regulatory requirements.
A PhD in Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Computer Science, or a related discipline will be considered a significant advantage.
Professional Certifications
The candidate must possess at least one internationally recognized professional certification relevant to IT governance, cybersecurity, information systems auditing or technology risk management. A second complementary certification is strongly preferred.
At least one relevant certification, such as CGEIT, CISA, CISM, CRISC or CISSP, demonstrating competence in governance, assurance, risk or information security.
Additional relevant credentials in IT service management (e.g., ITIL), COBIT, business continuity, cloud security, enterprise architecture, project management or Oracle technologies will be considered an advantage.
Certifications must be valid and verifiable, where applicable.
Professional Experience
The candidate must possess:
A minimum of 12 years of relevant IT experience, including at least five years in senior managerial or executive IT leadership roles and at least five years in banking or regulated financial services. The experience periods may overlap.
Demonstrated experience leading or overseeing large-scale, business-critical IT operations, including core banking or equivalent financial transaction systems, databases, networks, data centres, service management and operational resilience.
Proven experience in IT strategic planning, technology governance, cybersecurity, and enterprise risk management.
Substantial experience in managing complex IT projects, digital transformation initiatives, and technology modernization programmes.
Demonstrated experience in overseeing IT budgets, technology investments, procurement, and third-party technology service providers.
Experience in developing and implementing IT policies, procedures, internal controls, and information security frameworks.
Proven ability to provide strategic advice, independent oversight, and professional recommendations at senior executive or Board level.
Previous experience as a Chief Information Officer (CIO), Chief Technology Officer (CTO), IT Director, Head of IT or equivalent enterprise technology executive is strongly preferred. A Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) or IT assurance executive may be considered where demonstrable experience also covers enterprise IT operations, service delivery and core banking performance.
Experience working with international banking standards, regulatory frameworks, and information security requirements.
Demonstrated ability to interpret operational IT metrics, challenge technical root-cause analyses, assess recurring system outages and slowness, and evaluate whether permanent corrective actions and management accountability are effective.
Documented experience in improving service availability, transaction performance, incident resolution, service-level compliance or technology resilience in a regulated financial institution. Candidates shall be able to explain measurable outcomes from prior roles.
Priority will be given to those who have below additional expertise:
Previous membership of a Board of Directors, Board of Supervisors, or Board-level IT, Risk, or Audit Committee.
Oracle FLEXCUBE experience in upgrades, integration and performance oversight is strongly preferred. Experience with comparable core banking platforms is acceptable where transferable expertise is demonstrated.
Experience in international banking institutions or large financial organizations.
Experience in implementing or supervising core banking system transformations.
Knowledge of SWIFT, payment infrastructure, electronic money institutions, and digital financial services.
Familiarity with Basel Committee guidance on operational resilience and technology-related risks.
Personal and Leadership Competencies
The successful candidate must demonstrate:
Strong strategic thinking, analytical judgment, and independent decision-making capabilities.
Excellent understanding of corporate governance and Board-level responsibilities.
Ability to critically evaluate complex technological issues and communicate them effectively to non-technical Board members.
Strong leadership, professional integrity, and ethical standards.
Ability to maintain independence and exercise objective professional judgment.
Ability to anticipate emerging technology threats and assess their potential impact on the Bank.
Strong commitment to confidentiality, accountability, and the protection of the Bank's interests.
Sufficient time for report review, Board and committee meetings, material IT matters and ongoing professional development.
Independence from executive IT and material suppliers; disclosure of conflicts and recusal as required.

Submission Guidelines
Applicants who meet the above requirements should submit their updated Curriculum vitae (CV)/Resume to ( sr.recruitment-officer@ghazanfarbank.com )
please mention the Job Title and Vacancy Number in subject of your E-mail otherwise your Email will not be considered. Note only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for further recruitment process.
Appointment is subject to internal approvals, fit-and-proper assessment and DAB approval, including an interview if required. Corporate Secretary and Compliance shall verify the applicable appointment authority, eligibility and approval process before finalization.
The Nomination Committee should verify credentials, references and independence, and conduct a technical and governance interview using a case study on core banking slowness, outages, weak root-cause analysis and overdue remediation. The BoS shall assign committee duties under its charter and evaluate the member annually.

The role. Own the design and evolution of an area of the runtime, including trade-offs between model decisions at runtime and deterministic code, and between prompt/context fixes and structural ones.
Lead harness engineering at depth: long-running and durable execution, checkpoints and persistent plans, inline and multi-agent patterns, memory architecture, model swaps, and cost and latency control at scale.
Drive platformization: define the reusable components, shared libraries, intent routing, agent registry and integration patterns that let other teams build and integrate agents quickly, and drive adoption across teams.
Shape the multi-agent architecture and the convergence of existing and new agents into one experience.
Define how quality is measured and enforced: offline gating, online monitoring, and the prompt-analysis loop, working with AI Platform on the shared evals platform.
Own operational excellence for Smart Assist: on-call health, post-incident reviews, security posture (including prompt injection and permission-aware access), cost control, and entitlement and access correctness.

Partner with the EM, PMs, AI Experiences, AI Platform, MCP, and external partners on roadmap and dependencies.

5+ years building and operating production systems, with deep Python and strong system design (distributed systems, durable state and long-running workflows, APIs, data modeling).
2+ years building LLM agent systems in production, with real opinions from experience on context engineering, subagents, memory, tool design, async or deferred tools, and failure recovery.
Track record of designing evals that gate releases and of attributing production failures to the right layer (model, prompt, tool contract, context, environment), using calibrated LLM judges and online behavioral signals.
Experience building shared platforms or libraries that other teams adopt, and of influencing without authority.

title: AI Scientist - Entrepreneur in Residence
description:
Molecule is a decentralized science (DeSci) platform building the infrastructure to connect scientific research, blockchain technology, and funding. It empowers researchers and scientific communities to turn research discoveries into verifiable, fundable, and commercially valuable assets.
Through Molecule Labs, the platform provides tools for research data management, transparent record-keeping, secure collaboration, fundraising, and AI-powered research assessment. It also introduces a Coin-to-Company model, creating a structured pathway for token holders to potentially participate in the equity of companies built around scientific research.
By bridging science, and real-world commercialization, Molecule aims to make scientific research more transparent, accessible, collaborative, and economically sustainable.
The Role
You will be an AI Scientist at Molecule. In your first four weeks, you will live on-site, embedded with the founding team, and ship your first autonomous agent fleet into production against a real disease area. From day one you own the loop: design the agents, deploy them, pilot them, iterate, and generate scientific output that moves IP forward.
This is not a research role with a roadmap handed to you. You will pick targets, stand up infrastructure, recruit your sub-agents, and prove that autonomous science works at the bench-to-IP level. After the residency, you scale: more fleets, more disease areas, more shots on goal.
What You'll Do
Architect and deploy fleets of scientific agents spanning literature mining, target identification, molecular design, assay design, and data analysis
Pilot each fleet against a specific disease area and drive it to a tangible deliverable — a validated target, a candidate molecule, a novel dataset, an IP-NFT
Run multiple fleets in parallel across disease areas, reporting results directly to the CEO
Own the full stack: agent design, orchestration, evaluation, and scientific judgment on outputs
Define and set the standard for how autonomous science gets done at Molecule
Who You Are
Entrepreneurial to the core. You ship. You don't wait for permission.
Technically deep across LLMs, agent frameworks, and at least one wet-science domain - chemistry, biology, pharma, structural biology, or genomics
Comfortable with ambiguity. You may be the only person in the room who knows how to do what you do, and that energizes you
Credential-agnostic. PhD, MSc, BSc, or straight from high school - output matters, not titles. If you hold a degree, it should be from a top-tier institution (Oxbridge, Ivy League, MIT, Caltech, Stanford, ETH/EPFL, Imperial, or equivalent). If you skipped the degree, show us what you built instead.
All-in on intensity. Willing to live on-site for 4 weeks and operate at founder pace
What We Offer
An early seat at the company building the infrastructure for autonomous science
Direct ownership over a frontier no one else is running at
The fastest path from idea to deployed IP that exists in biotech today
We are an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to equality and weaving a community that values diverse perspectives and experiences and are actively seeking a diverse pool of applicants. All employment decisions are made without regard to race, colour, national origin, ancestry, sex, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, genetic information, religion, disability, medical condition, pregnancy, marital status, family status, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Language Pair : English to Farsi
Domain : Information Technology (IT), AI Models & Software Localization
Experience Level : Experienced (2+ years in Linguistic QA or Linguistic Testing)

Work Environment: A reliable high-speed internet connection and a dedicated workspace suitable for remote, independent contract work.

Check out this Loom video for more details:
We're looking for highly experienced software engineer (SR+) to help evaluate the quality of interactions with modern coding agents such as OpenAI Codex and Claude Code.
This is not a traditional engineering role. You won't be writing production code. You'll be evaluating something harder: whether the model thinks like a great engineer.
What this role actually is
You will assess how AI coding agents behave in real-world scenarios, focusing on:
• Whether the response makes sense
Whether the preamble and reasoning are useful
Whether the output reflects strong engineering judgment
Whether the interaction feels right to an experienced developer
This role is about engineering taste. Syntax correctness is the easy part.
What you'll be doing
Evaluate AI-generated coding interactions end to end
Judge whether outputs are useful, correct at a high level, and aligned with how a strong engineer would think
Assess the quality of explanations and reasoning, not just the code
Distinguish between levels of response quality (what makes something a 2 vs a 4)
Give clear, opinionated feedback in writing on what worked, what didn't, and what felt off or misleading
Help define what great looks like when working with tools like Cursor, Codex and Claude Code
What we mean by "taste"
We're looking for engineers who can answer questions like:
Does this feel like something a strong engineer would actually say?
Is this explanation helpful, or just technically correct?
Is the model guiding the user well, or just dumping output?
Would this interaction build or erode trust?
You should be comfortable making subjective but rigorous judgments, and explaining them clearly.
Who you are
Senior, Staff or Principal-level engineer (or equivalent experience)
Strong background in TypeScript/JavaScript or Python
Hands-on experience with at least one of OpenAI Codex, Claude Code or Cursor
Deep familiarity with modern AI-assisted dev workflows
Able to evaluate code without executing it or reviewing every line
Strong written and spoken English (B2 or above). You'll be writing detailed feedback and recording short video explanations, so this is a hard requirement
Comfortable giving direct, opinionated feedback
High bar for what good engineering looks like
Nice to have
Prior exposure to prompt design or evaluation workflows
Experience mentoring senior engineers or defining engineering standards
Engagement details
Rate: $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location
• Hours: 10-20 hours/week, flexible
Duration: ongoing. Projects run from about two weeks to a few months each, and we offer new ones to evaluators who do well
Start: as soon as you clear the take-home and a project has an open seat

description:
Role Title: Mechanical Design Engineer — Semiconductor & Vacuum Hardware
Role Type: Contractor
Location: Fully remote
Opportunity Snapshot
Pay: $90 -$155/hour
Duration: Initial phase of 20 part packages; production phase to follow
Location: Fully remote, no geographic restrictions
You'll need: 5+ years designing CNC-machined production parts, technical decision authority, and access to parametric CAD software
Your tasks: Author original CAD part packages, and peer review packages from other engineers
micro1 is engaging senior mechanical design engineers to create original CAD part packages for a client project in semiconductor and vacuum hardware. Your engineering judgment is what matters here — no prior AI experience required.
Each package is a new part you design from scratch: a difficult, high-value CNC part with a specific machining challenge, backed by a drawing with full GD&T, a design rationale, and a production scenario you justify from experience. Every part is independently reviewed by three other engineers, and you'll review others' work as well.
What you'll do
Design original parts in parametric CAD, delivered as native files plus STEP.
Produce the technical drawing: dimensions, tolerances, GD&T and datums, material and condition, finish, revision, drawing standard.
Write the design context: intended function, interfaces, operating conditions, the machining challenge, and your material and process rationale.
Build the production scenario: estimated unit cost and drivers, CNC cycle and setup hours, assumed volume, sourcing difficulty and lead time — with the engineering basis for each estimate.
Peer review other engineers' packages against technical quality, production realism, and engineering value, with part-specific evidence for every score.
Revise your own packages against review findings.
What we're looking for
5+ years of production engineering experience with comparable CNC parts, materials and processes in semiconductor or vacuum hardware.
Technical decision authority: you owned or approved critical design choices — drawing, tolerance or material approval, production release, or enforcing engineering quality standards. Design leads, principal and staff engineers, and technical authorities are the profile.
Experience at OEMs or specialist suppliers whose engineering standards you can reproduce.
Strong GD&T and tolerancing judgment, including cost and inspection implications.
Access to parametric CAD software (SolidWorks, NX, CATIA, Creo or similar) and the ability to deliver native files plus STEP.
Industry experience, not academic.
Important: originality and IP
Every design must be your own original work. You cannot use designs owned by a current or former employer or customer, and you cannot substitute public or purchased CAD. All deliverables become the client's property. If you're currently employed, check your employment agreement regarding outside work and invention assignment before applying.
How the selection process works
Apply and complete the screening questions

Profile review, including evidence of comparable parts and decisions owned
Onboarding — our Talent Ops team will get you set up

Location: Fully remote, no geographic restrictions
You'll need: 5+ years designing CNC-machined production parts, technical decision authority, and access to parametric CAD software
Your tasks: Author original CAD part packages, and peer review packages from other engineers
Your engineering judgment is what matters here — no prior AI experience required.
Each package is a new part you design from scratch: a difficult, high-value CNC part with a specific machining challenge, backed by a drawing with full GD&T, a design rationale, and a production scenario you justify from experience. Every part is independently reviewed by three other engineers, and you'll review others' work as well.
Required Skills
Design for manufacturing
Vacuum systems
Semiconductor equipment
Solidworks
Cnc part design
What you'll do
Design original parts in parametric CAD, delivered as native files plus STEP.
Produce the technical drawing: dimensions, tolerances, GD&T and datums, material and condition, finish, revision, drawing standard.
Write the design context: intended function, interfaces, operating conditions, the machining challenge, and your material and process rationale.
Build the production scenario: estimated unit cost and drivers, CNC cycle and setup hours, assumed volume, sourcing difficulty and lead time — with the engineering basis for each estimate.
Peer review other engineers' packages against technical quality, production realism, and engineering value, with part-specific evidence for every score.
Revise your own packages against review findings.
What we're looking for
5+ years of production engineering experience with comparable CNC parts, materials and processes in semiconductor or vacuum hardware.
Technical decision authority: you owned or approved critical design choices — drawing, tolerance or material approval, production release, or enforcing engineering quality standards. Design leads, principal and staff engineers, and technical authorities are the profile.
Experience at OEMs or specialist suppliers whose engineering standards you can reproduce.
Strong GD&T and tolerancing judgment, including cost and inspection implications.
Access to parametric CAD software (SolidWorks, NX, CATIA, Creo or similar) and the ability to deliver native files plus STEP.
Industry experience, not academic.
Important: originality and IP
Every design must be your own original work. You cannot use designs owned by a current or former employer or customer, and you cannot substitute public or purchased CAD. All deliverables become the client's property. If you're currently employed, check your employment agreement regarding outside work and invention assignment before applying.

description:
RevenueBase:
We're building the data infrastructure that makes AI agents trustworthy instead of error-prone.
We provide continuously refreshed, verified B2B data for autonomous AI agents and GTM workflows.
We've tripled growth while maintaining 100% gross dollar retention and staying cashflow positive.
We power AI agents for Clay, Zoominfo, Dun & Bradstreet, and the next generation of AI GTM tools.
Why We're Hiring This Role:
Our data platform is scaling rapidly, and we need engineer who can own pipelines end-to-end, keep data quality high, and ensure reliability as we grow.
This role exists to strengthen our data infrastructure, accelerate delivery through automation, and ensure our B2B customers receive accurate, timely data they can trust.
You'll work on data systems that directly power customer workflows - where pipeline reliability and data quality directly impact retention.
What You'll Do:
Build and maintain production-ready data pipelines using DBT, Snowflake, and modern orchestration tools.
Own data engineering features end-to-end, from implementation through optimization and deployment.
Fix and improve existing pipelines - identify bottlenecks, resolve issues, and enhance performance.
Drive automation initiatives across the data stack to accelerate delivery and reduce manual interventions.
Provide 2nd line support for B2B customers - investigate data issues, clarify edge cases, and ensure customers can trust their data.
Design and implement new data import pipelines as we expand our data source coverage.
Implement data quality improvements - validation, monitoring, and testing to ensure reliable, accurate data delivery.
Contribute to code reviews, architectural discussions, and data engineering best practices.
Who You Are:
You have 3+ years of professional data engineering experience.
Strong fundamentals in SQL, data modeling, Python and ETL/ELT principles.
Must have:
DBT - hands-on experience building and maintaining transformation pipelines
Nice to have:
Snowflake
Databricks
AWS (S3, Lambda, Glue, etc.)
Prefect or similar orchestration tools (Airflow, Dagster)
Solid understanding of data quality principles, testing strategies, and monitoring practices.
Comfortable working in a fast-moving, remote-first environment.
Strong communicator - able to explain technical issues clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Async-first mindset - can work independently, document decisions, and keep stakeholders informed without constant synchronous communication.
End-to-end ownership mentality - you see tasks through from planning to production, handling blockers and follow-through.
You care about data quality, pipeline reliability, and long-term maintainability.
Why RevenueBase:
Product with real traction: Customers rely on our platform in production.
High ownership: Small team where your work directly shapes the product.
Engineering-driven culture: Quality and correctness matter.
Growth stage company: Clear product-market fit and momentum.
Impact over process: Less bureaucracy, more building.
What We Offer:
Competitive compensation based on experience.
Meaningful ownership and long-term growth opportunities.
Flexible working hours.
Fully remote-friendly team.
Direct collaboration with founders and core engineering leadership.

title: Data Operations Associate, Expert Talent Pool
description:
About the Role
Join an expert network supporting human-data projects for AI research. You will source, curate, and validate data used to train and evaluate AI systems, with project assignments based on your experience.
What You'll Do
Source and collect documents, images, audio, or video according to project specifications, including capturing new media when requested.
Sort, deduplicate, tag, and filter datasets to meet quality standards.
Create synthetic examples and validate them against project guidelines.
Review annotations and determine whether they are correct, incorrect, or unclear.
Run calibration and audit rounds to support consistent annotation quality.
Help write and refine labeling guidelines with clear examples.
What We're Looking For
Zero to five years of experience in data work, research assistance, quality assurance, operations, content review, or a similar detail-focused role.
Experience sourcing, collecting, cleaning, or curating data, and checking work against written guidelines or specifications.
Comfort with Excel or Google Sheets and web-based tools; experience with annotation platforms such as Label Studio, Labelbox, CVAT, Scale, or Appen is a plus.
Clear written English and strong attention to detail; fluency in another language is a plus.
Relevant study or experience in fields such as statistics, linguistics, information science, computer science, library science, or GIS is valued.
Experience with AI data labeling, evaluation, synthetic data generation, or guideline writing is a plus.
Compensation & Benefits
$20 to $40 per hour, depending on project, field, and experience level. Payment is for hours worked.
Location
Fully remote. Projects may last from one week to several months.

title: Software Engineer - Backend | Global, Remote - Contract
description:
Role Title: Software Engineer - Backend
Role Type : Contractor (~15 hrs a week)
Location: Global, Fully remote
Time per task: 5 hours for trainers and 1.5 hours for reviewers
Engagement: Project-based — paid per approved task
Commitment: ~15 hours per week
Required Skills: Python3, Java, Rust, Algorithms, Basics C++, Typescript, Bug fixing, Feature implementation, Codebase refactoring, Performance optimization
You’ll need: Hands-on expertise in at least one of Python, Java, Rust, Go, C++, or TypeScript
Your tasks: Build challenging coding problems from real repositories, with reproducible environments and verifiers
You’ll create Reinforcement Learning Environments that test a model’s ability to solve real software engineering problems: tracking down subtle bugs, building non-trivial features, refactoring, and optimizing performance. Each task means defining the problem, building a reproducible environment, and writing a reference solution.
Scope of Work
Create realistic, challenging coding tasks for frontier AI models, drawn from repositories you know well.
Design problems that require real engineering skill — subtle bugs, non-trivial features, meaningful performance work — not lookup or boilerplate.
Build a reproducible environment for each task.
Write deterministic verifiers that accept correct solutions across different valid implementations, while rejecting incorrect, incomplete, or hard-coded approaches.
Provide a reference solution showing how the task can be solved.
Flag tasks that turn out to be ambiguous or unverifiable rather than submitting them.
Preferred Qualifications
Significant hands-on expertise in at least one of: Python3, Java, Rust, Go, C++, or TypeScript.
Deep understanding of algorithms, data structures, and software engineering principles.
Proven ability to debug complex systems, resolve bugs, and deliver effective optimizations.
Experience with large codebase refactoring and legacy system modernization.
Track record of delivering high-impact features from conception through delivery.
Strong documentation and communication skills to articulate technical concepts clearly.
Interest in AI and its technical challenges — previous AI experience not required.
Compensation Structure
Compensation is output-based; experts are paid per task that meets the project specifications. The time required may vary depending on your experience and workflow.
Start Timeline & Availability
We typically fill roles within 48 hours and are looking for experts ready to jump in right away. If selected, we expect you to start your first tasks within 24–48 hours of completing onboarding.
How the selection process works
Application
AI interview
Profile review, Hiring Manager
Onboarding

description:
Role Summary
Mozayel LLC, a US-registered company, is seeking a remote React Native (Expo) Developer to join its development team. The developer will be responsible for developing, maintaining and improving cross-platform mobile applications, managing day-to-day development of the apps and its backend, and ensuring a reliable user experience across Android and iOS.
You will serve as the primary developer, taking ownership of development and the codebase, implementing new features, fixing issues, and maintaining overall application performance. You will work closely with a QA tester and the company founder to plan, develop, test, and deliver updates.
Compensation is paid monthly in USD and will be determined based on experience and technical qualifications. Candidates will be asked to complete a paid trial task before receiving a final offer.

Duties and Responsibilities
Design and develop new mobile applications from the ground up for Android and iOS.
Build, maintain, and improve cross-platform applications using modern mobile development technologies.
Develop new features, improve existing functionality, troubleshoot technical issues, and resolve bugs.
Design, develop, and maintain backend systems, databases, APIs, and server-side functionality.
Develop web-based applications and administrative platforms.
Take ownership of the complete software development lifecycle, from initial planning and architecture to development, testing, and deployment.
Write clean, maintainable, scalable, and well-structured code.
Implement secure authentication, data management, access controls, and reliable data synchronization.
Ensure applications support multiple languages, internationalization (i18n), and right-to-left (RTL) layouts where required.
Maintain application stability, performance, security, and compatibility across devices.
Identify technical improvements, investigate complex problems, and implement effective solutions.
Follow professional software development practices, including version control, code reviews, testing, and documentation.
Collaborate with team members to plan development priorities, evaluate progress, and deliver reliable software.
Stay current with modern development technologies, tools, and industry best practices.

Job Requirements
Minimum 3 years of professional mobile application development experience.
Proven experience developing and publishing at least one React Native / Expo application on both Google Play and the Apple App Store. Applicants must provide links to previously published applications.
Strong proficiency in TypeScript, JavaScript, React, and React Native.
Practical experience building and maintaining backend systems, relational databases, APIs, and server-side functionality.
Experience with database design, security policies, migrations, and serverless functions. Familiarity with Supabase or equivalent backend platforms is required.
Solid understanding of Git, version control, branching strategies, code reviews, and continuous integration.
Experience developing responsive user interfaces and maintaining consistent application behavior across different devices.
Practical experience with internationalization (i18n), multilingual applications, and right-to-left (RTL) layouts.
Understanding of application security, performance optimization, debugging, and error monitoring.
Ability to independently develop new applications and take responsibility for technical decisions.
Good written and verbal English communication skills.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with mobile application build automation, application store submissions, and over-the-air updates.
Experience with offline-first applications and reliable data synchronization.
Experience with server-side document and PDF generation.
Familiarity with application monitoring, crash reporting, and performance analysis tools.
Knowledge of Dari or Pashto is an advantage.
Experience using AI-assisted development tools effectively to improve development productivity.
Experience working independently in remote development environments.

Submission Guidelines
Application Submission Guidelines
To be considered for this position, applicants must follow these submission requirements:
Attach one recent photograph with your application.
Send your application to business@mozayel.com .
Use AFM-SD-001 as the exact email subject line.
Important: All submission requirements must be followed. Applications that do not include a recent photograph or use the specified email subject line may be disqualified without further consideration.

description:
About Supabase
Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.
About the Role
We’re looking for a Data API Engineer to join our Data API Team and help improve the feature set, reliability and performance of our Data API, based on the PostgREST project.
This role is ideal for someone who thrives in async, fast-paced environments and is excited about building developer tools that scale to millions.
What You’ll Be Responsible For
Work on PostgREST’s PostgreSQL driver (based on Hasql) and remove bottlenecks and improve it’s performance.
Work on PostgREST development of new features and bug fixes, aligned towards the goal of a multitenant Data API.
Resolve incidents and escalated support issues, while also improving observability and performance.
Collaborate cross-functionally with other teams to debug and solve integration issues with the Supabase platform.
You Might Be a Good Fit If You
Strong Haskell skills with at least 3 years of experience.
Experience using the C language.
Solid knowledge of SQL and plpgsql scripting in PostgreSQL.
Strong track record of contributing to and engaging with open-source projects. Bonus points if you’ve maintained an open source project.
Strong experience with providing technical support to users with varying levels of technical expertise.
Experience with debugging applications under the Linux operating system.
What We Offer
Fully Remote
We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.
ESOP
Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.
Tech Allowance
Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.
Health Benefits
Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.
Annual Off-Sites
Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.
Flexible Work
We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.
Professional Development
Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.
About the Team
Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.
~400 team members
60+ countries
20+ languages spoken
Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)
540,000+ community members
We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

description:
Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. We have created a new career path at Canonical for Performance Engineers who bring exceptional clarity to software performance, correctness and efficiency. We are adding these roles to every engineering team at the company.
As an open source platform, we have teams that work at every level of the software stack - from the kernel up through server and desktop applications, all the way to the web. We are adding roles with this focus in every engineering team in the company, to act as drivers of performance engineering skills, tools, culture and insights to our entire product range . We have also created a central performance engineering team, where we will drive shared tools, dashboarding capabilities, measurement frameworks, analytical capabilities and skills. We call this career focus ' percorr ' because we have found that the same deep insights that enable sophisticated performance measurement and design also enable teams to improve their harnesses and frameworks for correctness. Understanding not only the application, but the runtime, the compiler, and the system, all the way down to the CPU, gives an engineer the ability to think creatively and with insight about the right things to measure, and the right ways to verify correctness. We have found that performance engineers will often improve the deepest and trickiest areas of our test harnesses, and unblock their teams to test and measure previously 'dark' aspects of their work.
We also have teams that work with every major silicon vendor and cloud, with a particular emphasis on performance optimisation of the entire stack for that architecture, CPU family or hypervisor. Our goal is to ensure that Ubuntu users can select whatever platform they want for their workloads and know they have access to the very best performance and efficiency across the entire stack from kernel to codec.
If they wish, we will enable performance and correctness engineers to move between products every two years, so that they have the opportunity to raise the bar for performance in an array of products over time, and also that teams have the benefit of fresh eyes on their processes, thinking, harnesses, dashboards and code. Our performance and correctness leads are expected to be truly exceptional individuals, and also leaders who are confident setting expectations of change, sharing insights and skills, running initiatives and programs. There is no way to move a meaningful codebase without also moving the people behind it.
This is a career path for perfectionists and precision artists. Whether you have a particular language focus - C, C++, Rust, Golang, Python, Java, Flutter-Dart or others - or a particular love of the kernel or hardware or CPU instruction set, whether you see yourself as driving perceived user experience through performance or optimising the efficiency of data centers to reduce carbon footprint, this process is the best way to find a role at Canonical that speaks to your precision, rigour, insight and drive.

title: Platform Engineer - Compute Capacity
description:
About Supabase
Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.
About the Role
We are seeking a platform engineer to join our Compute Capacity team. This team owns the capacity plan that keeps compute supply ahead of demand across every region we operate in — the forecasting, buffer policy, and provisioning systems that make sure a project never runs into a wall it didn't know was there.
You'll work on the systems that turn a capacity plan into provisioned reality: reservation acquisition, fleet reconciliation, and the automation that keeps what we've committed to in sync with what we're actually running. You'll help build the metrics and alerting that let capacity problems surface months out, on vendor lead time, rather than at the moment someone needs the room.
You'll design, build, and operate systems that are both robust and highly automated — helping us hold the right buffer at the right cost, catch drift before it becomes a shortage, and give every team a single, trustworthy view of how much room we have across the millions of databases we manage.
What You'll Be Responsible For
Help build and maintain the capacity plan that keeps Supabase's compute supply ahead of demand across regions and instance families
Support buffer policy by modeling headroom targets and their cost tradeoffs for review and sign-off
Build and maintain automation that turns the capacity plan into provisioned reality — reservation acquisition and top-up, fleet reconciliation, drift detection between committed and running capacity
Extend our infrastructure as code for capacity-relevant provisioning
Instrument capacity: build and maintain metrics for saturation, reservation coverage, idle buffer, forecast error, and provisioning latency
Build and tune capacity alerting so headroom, quota, and reservation issues surface months out rather than at the moment of impact
Support the demand gate — helping intake large customer commitments, launches, migrations, and new regions so they reach the plan before they reach the fleet
Contribute to mitigation projects: right-sizing, instance-family migrations, autoscaling improvements, workload consolidation
Help drive down compute cost per database through right-sizing, placement, and commitment coverage work
Participate in capacity incident response and post-incident follow-through
You Might Be A Good Fit If You
Have 5+ years across infrastructure engineering, SRE, platform, or capacity engineering, ideally at SaaS or cloud infrastructure scale
Have production software engineering experience — you've owned and operated a service , not just a notebook. Comfortable in modern languages like TypeScript, Python , and Go
Are comfortable working against forecasts and assumptions that are incomplete, and can revise your work as those assumptions change
Have experience with Infrastructure as Code (Pulumi or Terraform)
Have built or maintained observability for systems you own — metrics that answer real questions and alerting people trust (Prometheus/Grafana, CloudWatch, or similar);
Have solid working knowledge of AWS EC2 : instance families and generations, purchase options, capacity reservations, and quota mechanics
Have some financial fluency — you understand reservation economics and the basic tradeoffs between coverage, utilization, and cost
Communicate clearly across audiences, from engineers to finance stakeholders
What We Offer
Fully Remote
We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.
ESOP
Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

title: Piping Engineer (Oil & Gas) — Pipeline Routing, Flow Analysis, AutoCAD
description:
Looking for a piping engineer to support an oil and gas programme for a European energy company. Project-based, paid per assignment, no office hours.

THE PROGRAMME

Pipelines moving product from one point to the next — A to B, B to C. We need someone who has actually done this: routing lines, sizing them, and knowing when a design will fail at the fabrication yard or at inspection.

WHAT YOU WILL BE ASKED TO DO

Review pipeline routing, isometrics and P&IDs, and give comments that a design team can act on the same day.
Run line sizing and hydraulic checks — flow rate, pressure drop, velocity, surge where it matters.
Specify pipe grade, wall thickness, valves, flanges and supports.
Mark up drawings in AutoCAD; produce a clean issue sheet of comments.
Visit a site or fabrication yard when the assignment calls for it.
Write short English memos — usually two pages, sometimes less.

WHAT WE NEED FROM YOU

Native Persian speaker, comfortable working with Persian-speaking engineers and suppliers.
Direct experience on Iranian or Middle East oil and gas pipeline projects. We are not looking for someone who has only read about them.
Based in China and able to meet face to face. We will want to sit down with you, not just call.
English strong enough for a technical call and a written memo.
Available on a project basis — this is freelance, not a permanent post.

TOOLS

AutoCAD is required. Hydraulic calculation — your own spreadsheet is fine, we care about the result, not the software. Familiarity with ASME B31.3/B31.4/B31.8 is expected.

HOW THE WORK IS STRUCTURED

Milestones by assignment. Scope, deliverables and fee agreed in writing before each piece of work starts.
Typical assignment: a few days to a few weeks. Repeat work is likely for the right person.
Travel, if needed, is arranged and paid by the client.

HOW TO BID

Tell us: the biggest pipeline job you handled (diameter, length, what it carried), one design problem you caught before it reached the yard, and your rate per assignment. Bid with your own number — we are comparing engineers, not haggling.

title: Cloud Platform Engineer
description:
About the Role
As a Cloud Platform Engineer at Supabase, you’ll join Cloud Engineering, part of Engineering Operations, and shape the foundations that let engineering teams build, ship, and operate infrastructure safely and independently across AWS and GCP.
This is a role spanning cloud governance, platform engineering, and hands-on operations. You’ll work across AWS and GCP account structure, identity and access management, Infrastructure as Code (IaC), reusable platform primitives, security boundaries, and self-service workflows for engineers.
You’ll be joining at a point where many of these foundations are being actively defined or reworked. We’re looking for someone who can take ambiguous, messy, business-critical infrastructure problems and turn them into pragmatic systems, tools, standards, and written guidance that scale with the company and empower teams to go faster.
What You’ll Be Responsible For
Designing and implementing cloud governance across AWS and GCP, including identity, account organization, access controls, and guardrails.
Building reusable infrastructure and building blocks using Infrastructure as Code (IaC), enabling teams to provision and manage infrastructure safely and consistently.
Creating self-service capabilities that reduce organizational friction and let engineers move more quickly within sensible boundaries.
Owning resource governance and visibility: management tagging, a trustworthy inventory of what exists and who owns it, and consistent cross-account billing data.
Developing reusable security primitives, including secrets storage, KMS, certificate management, token vending, direct service-to-service authentication, mTLS, and related platform services.
Owning cloud-level network and operational primitives: IP address management, DNS, and health signals such as service-limit and quota alerting.
Combining software engineering with hands-on operations and total ownership: building, deploying, monitoring, troubleshooting, and improving what you own.
Establishing and sharing cloud engineering best practices through documentation, internal tooling, examples, and enablement.
You Might Be a Good Fit If You
Have 5+ years of experience in cloud governance, platform engineering, and/or operations, have operated production systems at scale, and carried on-call for them.
Have previously undertaken a significant migration, e.g. rearchitected an AWS account topology, introduced IaC for existing infrastructure, centralized identity/SSO, or brought a second cloud under governance.
Enjoy building internal platform and self-service experiences for other engineers.
Are genuinely deep in at least one—ideally two—of the three strength areas below (and tell us which is your center of gravity):
Tooling & ecosystem: You’re intimately familiar with the breadth of AWS services in general, and IAM/SSO in particular. You know their Well-Architected Framework, and when to reach outside. location: Afghanistan | Burundi | Central African Republic | Colombia | Congo DRC | Germany | Iraq | Jordan | Lebanon | palestine | Sweden | South Sudan | Syria | Uganda | Ukraine | Yemen

description:
War Child is looking for:
A dedicated and talented QA Engineer with at least 3 years of experience to join our team in developing the Can’t Wait to Learn game. The ideal candidate is highly detail-oriented and passionate about ensuring product stability and quality. You will be responsible for testing, documenting, and ensuring that the game meets the highest standards of quality and performance. Your role will be critical in identifying potential issues, ensuring seamless user experiences, and maintaining a stable and reliable product for children.
Project Overview:
The *Can’t Wait to Learn* (CWTL) project is a pioneering initiative that leverages technology to deliver high-quality education to children in conflict-affected areas. The project uses digital game-based learning to provide children with access to effective and engaging educational resources, even in challenging environments.
Your Mission:
· Manual Testing: Perform manual testing of the product with a proactive approach to identify bugs and ensure stability across various platforms and devices.
· Bug Reporting: Identify, document, and communicate bugs effectively to developers using tracking tools such as Jira, ensuring that issues are addressed promptly.
· Test Documentation: Create and maintain test cases, bug reports, and other documentation to support the QA process and provide clear visibility of test results.
· Automated Testing: Develop and maintain automated tests using frameworks such as Vitest and Jest to improve testing efficiency and coverage.
· Unity Testing: Write and execute tests specifically for Unity applications to ensure functionality, performance, and usability.(optional)
· Creative Testing Approaches: Identify unconventional usage patterns, edge cases, and potential scenarios to test for non-obvious bugs and inconsistencies.
· Team Collaboration: Work closely with developers, designers, and other stakeholders to understand project requirements and provide QA insights during development.
· Content Integration: Support testing and validation of graphic content imported into Unity, ensuring that assets are correctly integrated and displayed.
· Release Process Oversight: Collaborate with the development team to understand the release process, validate deployments, and ensure quality before releases.
· Analytical Tools: Utilize analytics tools and methods to support testing with data-driven insights and assess product performance post-release.
Your Profile:
· Experience: At least 3+ years of experience as a QA Engineer, preferably in the gaming or educational technology sectors.
· Testing Frameworks: Hands-on experience with testing frameworks such as Vitest and Jest.
· Unity Expertise: Experience testing and validating Unity-based applications is highly preferred.
· Technical Skills: Familiarity with JavaScript or C# for writing automated tests.(optional)
· Documentation & Reporting: Strong skills in documenting and reporting bugs, test cases, and other QA-related activities using tools such as Jira or TestRail.
· Analytical Mindset: Ability to identify not only current issues but also anticipate future problems based on observed patterns and system behavior.
· Communication Skills: Excellent communication skills with the ability to work effectively in a collaborative team environment.
· Attention to Detail: A keen eye for detail, ensuring that the smallest issues are identified and addressed before product release.
· Languages: Proficiency in English and Ukrainian (both written and spoken).
Preferred Qualifications:
· Team Management: Experience in managing a QA team or leading QA efforts is a plus.
· Game Release Process: Understanding of the game deployment process and experience working with developer accounts for game submissions.
· Graphic Content Integration: Familiarity with importing and validating graphic content within Unity.
· Analytical Tools Experience: Experience working with analytical tools to support QA efforts.
· Humanitarian Experience: Prior experience working in humanitarian or educational projects, especially those targeted at children.
Tools & Technologies:
· Primary: Unity, C#, JavaScript, Vitest, Jest, Jira, TestRail
· Project Management: Jira, Confluence
· Design Collaboration: Miro, Figma
What We Offer:
· Location : We work with global teams with team members being based in different locations. War Child is based in Afghanistan, Burundi, the Central African Republic, Colombia, DR Congo, Germany, Iraq, Jordan, Lebanon, the occupied Palestinian territory, South Sudan, Sweden, Syria, Uganda, Ukraine and Yemen. Preference is given to applicants who reside and have valid working permits. War Child does not offer relocation.
· Salary and benefits are in line with your residing country and contracting office, we offer local packages.
· Professional Development : Opportunities for capacity building and growth, both within the role and through War Child’s broader network.
· Meaningful Impact : The chance to make a tangible difference in the lives of children and families affected by conflict, contributing to long-term, sustainable change.
· Equal Opportunities : War Child is an inclusive employer committed to diversity and inclusion, respecting all individuals regardless of age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, or physical ability.
· Workplace Culture : War Child is dedicated to fostering a diverse, inclusive, and respectful workplace that prioritizes safety and fairness for all individuals. We strictly prohibit any form of discrimination, harassment, retaliation, or bullying within our organization
Why You Should Apply
· Make a Real Impact: Your work will directly contribute to providing quality education to children who need it most, creating lasting change in their lives.
· Career Growth : Join a dynamic organization that values your professional development and offers opportunities for learning, growth, and innovation.
· Global Reach: Play a key role in scaling a ground-breaking programme that operates in multiple conflict-affected regions around the world.
· Collaborative and Mission-Driven: Work alongside passionate colleagues and partners united in a mission to protect children and help them thrive despite adversity .
How to Apply
Qualified candidates are encouraged to submit their applications by January 1, 2025 . We are reviewing submissions on a rolling basis, so early applications are strongly recommended.
____________________________________________________________________________________
By submitting your application you certify that all of the statements made in your application are true, complete, and correct and are made in good faith. You understand that falsifying, misrepresenting or intentionally withholding information will be grounds for rejection of your application or withdrawal of any offer of appointment or, if an appointment offer has been accepted, this will be ground for employment sanctions, such as, but not limited to, instant dismissal. In addition, you understand that you need to submit a Criminal Record Certificate and that, if you fail to submit it, no employment relationship can be established.
War Child is an international organisation, and we are committed to be a diverse and inclusive employer, placing human and child rights at the centre of our existence and work. We hire our new colleagues based on their talents, competences and shared values; we do not distinguish them based on their age, gender and gender identity, race, color, ethnicity, religion, culture, sexual orientation, disability etc.
The safety of children and youth is a paramount and essential to War Child’s work. War Child has a zero tolerance policy towards any form of abuse. To prevent placing children and youth at any risk this subject is addressed in our recruitment and selection procedures. Moreover, the accepted candidates will be required to state their commitment/ intent to be aware, consider and adhere to the minimum standards applicable in development and humanitarian settings, such as humanitarian values and principles, Sphere Humanitarian Charter, Standards in the Humanitarian Standards Partnership, Core Humanitarian Standard, International Humanitarian Law, Code of Conduct for the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement and Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) in Disaster Relief and IASC Six Core Principles Relating to Sexual Exploitation and Abuse.
Disclaimer
· Only applications received via our website are processed.
· If we appoint a suitable candidate before the given closing date, we reserve the right to remove the vacancy from our website before that date. In such a case, any responses received after that time are not processed.
· It could be that during our selection process the closing date for the vacancy is extended. If so, and you have not yet heard from us, your application will remain active.
About War Child :
The War Child Alliance is an international non-governmental organization committed to providing psychosocial support, child protection, youth empowerment programming and quality education to the children affected by armed conflict. We implement evidence-based interventions to empower key stakeholders—including governments, educators, caregivers, and communities—to foster children’s wellbeing, education, and self-determination. War Child has a presence in 19 countries: Jordan, Lebanon, the occupied Palestinian territory, Syria, Iraq, Yemen, Afghanistan, Colombia, Burundi, DR Congo, the Central African Republic, South Sudan, Uganda, Ukraine, Germany, Sweden, The Netherlands, United Kingdom and the United States of America.
Learn more about War Child and our programmes https://www.warchild.net/
Safeguarding
War Child is committed to humanitarian values, standards and norms and we expect the same from job applicants. War Child is especially committed to safeguarding the children and youth we support and doesn’t tolerate any form of abuse. Because we want to prevent and deter any actions that place children and youth at risk, conduct references are an important part of our recruitment procedure. As part of the selection process, War Child will request standardized references in accordance with the Inter-Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme and a recent Criminal Records statement.
